subject: Climate & Environment
title: Seed Banks and Genetic Rescue
description: A micro-lesson that makes Seed Banks and Genetic Rescue usable.

hook.text: Deep inside an Arctic mountain, a vault holds seeds from nearly every food crop on Earth.

buildup.text: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault stores over 1.3 million seed samples from around the world.

discovery.text: Seed banks preserve genetic diversity that could save crops from future diseases or climate shifts.

twist.text: Syria's gene bank was destroyed in war. Svalbard's backup allowed them to rebuild it entirely.

climax.text: Frozen zoos now store DNA, sperm, and embryos of endangered animals for possible future revival.

punchline.text: Saving seeds today is insurance against disasters we can't yet imagine.

quiz.question: What is stored in the Svalbard Global Seed Vault?
options: Seeds from nearly every food crop on Earth

details.summary: Seed banks preserve plant genetic material in cold storage as insurance against extinction, crop failure, and climate change. The Svalbard Global Seed Vault holds over 1.1 million seed samples from virtually every country on Earth.
details.whyItMatters: Genetic rescue preserves options for the future. Seed banks are the ultimate backup for crops and wild plants, safeguarding diversity that cannot be recreated once lost.
takeaways: Svalbard stores over 1.1 million seed samples from around the world
Seeds are stored at minus 18 degrees Celsius for long-term viability
Genetic rescue has helped restore inbred wildlife populations

faq.question: What is the Svalbard Global Seed Vault?
faq.answer: Built into a mountain on a Norwegian Arctic island, Svalbard stores backup copies of seeds from gene banks worldwide. Permafrost and thick rock provide natural refrigeration, and the vault is designed to withstand centuries of climate change and conflict.

faq.question: How does genetic rescue save endangered wildlife?
faq.answer: When an isolated population becomes dangerously inbred, introducing individuals or genetic material from genetically distinct populations restores variation. This was used to save the Florida panther from inbreeding depression by introducing Texas cougars.
